question: Fed decreases interest rates by 50+ bps after January 2026 meeting?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's January 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for January 27 - 28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their January meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

subquestions.question: Will the target federal funds rate be changed by 25 basis points or more at the Federal Reserve's October 2025 meeting?
subquestions.background_information: During the October 2025 FOMC meeting, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) is scheduled to make decisions on the target federal funds rate. Recent reports indicate a possibility of further rate cuts, with expectations of a 93.2% probability of a 25‑bps cut at the October meeting. The decision to change the federal funds rate is of significance as it may indicate the FED's approach to stimulating economic growth or managing inflation. This decision could provide valuable insight into the likelihood of a 50+ bps cut after January 2026.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves positively if the Federal Reserve's announcement regarding the target federal funds rate for the meeting on October 2025 indicates a change of 25 basis points or more, as reported on the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm. It resolves negatively if no such change is reported. The resolution date for this question is October 18, 2025 (inclusive).
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is relevant as it aligns with the timeline of the ultimate question and serves as an early indicator of the likelihood of a significant rate cut by the FED after January 2026.

question: US recession in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes”, if either of the following conditions are met:

1.  The National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) publicly announces that a recession has occurred in the United States, at any point in 2025, with the announcement made by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

2.  The seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly U.S. real GDP from the previous quarter is less than 0.0 for two consecutive quarters between Q4 2024 and Q4 2025 (inclusive), as reported by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). 

Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

Note that advance estimates will be considered. For example, if upon release, the advance estimate for Q2 2025 was negative, and the Q1 2025's most recent, up-to-date estimate was also negative, this market would resolve to "Yes". If on December 31, 2025 the latest estimate for quarterly GDP in Q3 2025 was negative, this market will stay open until the Advance estimate of Q4 2025 is published, at which point it will resolve to "Yes" if Q4 2025 was negative or if the NBER declares a recession by then.

The resolution source will be the official announcements from the NBER and the BEA’s estimate of seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly US real GDP from previous quarters as released by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

subquestions.question: Will the National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) publicly announce that a recession has occurred in the United States by September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The NBER is the official organization responsible for dating the start and end of recessions in the United States. Their announcements are widely recognized as authoritative. The current state of the economy is uncertain, with conflicting signals such as negative quarterly GDP growth, declining corporate profits, and increased downside risks to employment and economic growth. There is also increased uncertainty due to tariff policies and legal rulings. Various reports and economic experts have differing opinions on the likelihood and severity of a 2025 recession.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves positively if the NBER publicly announces that a recession has occurred in the United States by September 30, 2025 (11:59 PM ET). The resolution source will be the official announcement from the NBER, available at https://www.nber.org/
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant as the definitive announcement by NBER would provide a clear indication of whether a recession has occurred before the end of 2025, serving as an early indicator of the ultimate question.

question: US strikes Iran by June 30, 2026?
description:

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US military forces that impact Iranian ground territory or any official Iranian embassy or consulate (e.g., if a weapons depot on Iranian soil is hit by an US missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether they land on Iranian territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves positively if credible mainstream media sources or official government statements confirm that the US government issued a public statement explicitly citing Iranian missile or drone attacks as a threat before January 22, 2026. The statement should be verifiable from reputable news outlets or official government communication. Inconclusive reports or unofficial sources will not be counted as sufficient evidence. Example sources include statements from the White House, State Department, Department of Defense, or major news outlets such as CNN, BBC, Reuters, or the Associated Press.
subquestions.rationale: If the US government publicly acknowledges Iranian missile or drone attacks as a threat, it suggests an increasing likelihood of taking military action against Iran, making this an important indicator for the ultimate question.

question: US x Venezuela military engagement by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela between August 21, and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count toward a "Yes" resolution; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not. 

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

These actions suggest a potential for direct military confrontation.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves positively if there is a direct military confrontation involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela in the Caribbean before October 1, 2025 (inclusive). question: Will Tesla launch a driverless Robotaxi service by October 31?
description:

Any service that allows a member of the general public to summon and ride in a Tesla vehicle operating without any human—onboard or remote—actively controlling the vehicle will count. A human may be present in the vehicle or monitoring remotely for emergency intervention, but they must not be physically positioned to take control (for example, no safety driver in the driver’s seat) and must not actively steer, brake, accelerate, or otherwise drive the car under normal operation.

A program that is restricted to Tesla employees, invite-only testers, closed-beta participants, factory self-delivery features, or the mere release of Full Self-Driving software for private owner-drivers will not qualify. Regulatory permits or approvals, press demonstrations, and prototype unveilings without live public ridership likewise will not count toward resolution.

However, there are concerns about Tesla's reliance on camera systems and lack of comprehensive autonomous driving capability, and regulatory approvals remain a potential obstacle.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Tesla publicly launches a fully driverless taxi service, which is accessible to the general public, in the San Francisco Bay Area by September 8, 2025, 11:59 PM UTC. The launch must allow a member of the general public to summon and ride in a Tesla vehicle operating without any human actively controlling the vehicle, with no safety driver in the driver’s seat and no active human steering, braking, accelerating, or driving under normal operation. The resolution will be determined by official announcements from Tesla or reputable news sources reporting the public launch.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question as it focuses on the specific launch of a fully driverless Robotaxi service by Tesla in a particular area. The resolution of this question will provide valuable insights into Tesla's progress with their autonomous ride-hailing service, thereby serving as an important early indicator of their ability to meet the ultimate question's deadline.

The September 8, 1995, “Agreed Basic Principles” between Bosnia and Yugoslavia, which recognized the borders and sovereignty of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and was later formalized through the Dayton Peace Agreement, is an example of a qualifying agreement.

The April 19, 2013, Brussels Agreement between Serbia and Kosovo, in which Serbia recognized Kosovo’s de facto administration but did not formally grant de jure recognition, would not be considered a qualifying agreement under this market, as this market requires formal recognition of sovereignty rather than acknowledgment of administrative control.

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

question: Will the ECB announce no change at the February 2026 meeting?

question: 5kt meteor strike in 2025?
description:

The relevant field for determining impact energy is the “Impact Energy (kt)” column. If this dataset has not been updated to include all relevant dates by February 28, 2026, or if the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository becomes permanently unavailable, this market may resolve based on a consensus of credible sources including the European Space Agency (ESA), the International Asteroid Warning Network (IAWN), the U.S. Department of Defense, or credible reporting of a scientific consensus, such as a NASA press release.

subquestions.background_information: On August 19, 2025, a bright fireball struck the night sky over southern Japan, releasing an estimated 1.6 kilotons of energy as it disintegrated over the Pacific Ocean southeast of Kyushu. This event was considered considerably smaller yet noteworthy compared to the historic Chelyabinsk airburst in 2013, which released approximately 440 kilotons of energy. Preliminary analysis indicated an entry velocity of ~21 km/s, an entry angle of 58°, and a terminal altitude near 18 km, suggesting the fireball most likely broke apart over the ocean. NASA's CNEOS reported a preliminary impact energy of about 1.6 kilotons of TNT equivalent with peak brightness near 30.9°N and 131.8°E.

The relevant field for determining impact energy will be the 'Impact Energy (kt)' column in the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository: https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/

Only official policy announcements will qualify.

Informal statements, plans contingent on future conditions, statements of intent without a formal policy directive, or any other statements that do not constitute a formal policy announcement will not be considered.

A consensus of credible reporting confirming that the “Board of Peace” or equivalent Gaza oversight board has been established, includes U.S. participation and is operational will also qualify.  

The resolution source will be official announcements from the Trump administration however a consensus for credible reporting may also be used.

The Board of Peace is intended to oversee the reconstruction and economic recovery of Gaza, with roles including appointing an intermediate executive committee and Palestinian technocrats for daily operations. The naming of members to the intermediate executive committee is a significant step towards the operationalization of the Board of Peace.

Source: [3] The Times of Israel, [8] Al Jazeera Online
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if the Trump administration formally announces the appointment of members to the intermediate executive committee for the Board of Peace by January 13, 2026. Official statements or credible reporting confirming the appointment will serve as qualifying evidence for resolution. If by January 13, 2026, no formal announcement is made by the Trump administration regarding the appointment of members to the intermediate executive committee, the question resolves 'No'.

Sources: [3] The Times of Israel (https://www.timesofisrael.com/us-expected-to-unveil-gaza-board-of-peace-in-late-december-around-trump-netanyahu-meeting-official-says/), [8] Al Jazeera Online (https://www.aljazeera.com/)
subquestions.rationale: The appointment of members to the intermediate executive committee for the Board of Peace is a crucial step towards operationalizing the proposed oversight board in Gaza. It serves as an early indicator of progress in the establishment of the Board of Peace, thus providing valuable evidence relevant to the ultimate question.

question: Will Pope Leo visit another country first?

Whether or not Pope Leo XIV enters the country's airspace or maritime territory during the timeframe of this market will have no bearing on a positive resolution.

If Pope Leo XIV doesn't visit any country by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

Cardinal Bechara Boutros Rai, patriarch of the Maronite Catholic Church, has stated that preparations are underway for the visit, pending a Vatican decision. The Vatican has not officially confirmed the trip, but local church leaders have announced the expected visit, which is seen as an important symbol due to Lebanon's multicultural, multi-religious environment. The visit has been linked to Pope Leo XIV's anticipated trip to Turkey for the 1,700th anniversary of the Council of Nicaea, and it has significant implications for the Christian presence in the Middle East.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves positively if credible photographic or video evidence, or an official announcement from the Vatican, confirms that Pope Leo XIV physically entered the territorial borders of Lebanon between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31. Credible evidence can include widely recognized news sources or official Vatican announcements. The evidence must clearly indicate the date and location of the entry into Lebanon's territorial borders. The following sources will be used for resolution criteria: UPI (https://www.upi.com), Times of India (https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com), Yahoo (https://www.yahoo.com). subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question as the expected visit to Lebanon is a significant event that can serve as an early indicator of Pope Leo XIV's international travels. If the Pope visits Lebanon, it would provide strong evidence of his intention to conduct international trips, potentially influencing the resolution of the ultimate question.

question: Will China lift rare earths export ban by December 31?
description:

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Chinese government officially lifts, removes, or reduces any of the export restrictions placed on rare earth metals on April 4, between July 23 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

The issuance of a qualifying official act by China within this market's timeframe will count toward a "Yes" resolution, even if the lifting or reduction of the stated export ban does not come into effect until after this market's resolution date.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the government of the United States, however a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

subquestions.question: Will China increase the monthly rare earth products circulation reporting requirements by December 31?

Producers were required to record and submit monthly reports on the circulation of rare-earth products to a government-run tracking system. The rules took effect on July 28 and were part of the wider export restrictions on rare-earth metals imposed on April 4. The tightening of reporting requirements could signal ongoing strict control over the rare-earth industry, possibly indicating a lack of intent to relax export restrictions.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves positively if China imposes stricter monthly reporting requirements on the circulation of rare earth products, as officially reported by the Chinese government or through a consensus of credible reporting, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31. The primary source of information for resolution will be the official information from the government of the United States, while credible reporting can also serve as a resolution source.
subquestions.rationale: The increase in monthly rare earth products reporting requirements may signal China's intent to maintain strict control over the rare-earth industry, which could suggest a lack of immediate plans to lift export restrictions. Therefore, this question can serve as an indicator of the ultimate question regarding the lifting of rare earths export ban by China.

question: Will the Fed cut-pause-pause in 2025?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings in 2025 (September 16-17, October 28-29, and December 9-10).

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered. 

Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the December meeting by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.question: Will the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) announce a rate cut at its meeting on September 16-17, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Based on expert expectations and recent statements, there is an anticipation of a rate cut at the September FOMC meeting. Markets are currently expecting a September rate cut, with further cuts possible in October and December. The FOMC has held interest rates steady for the first five meetings of 2025, but recent job growth data and downward revisions to prior month's reports suggest a potential for a rate cut. The Committee's decision will be closely watched by financial markets and investors, and any announcement of a rate cut at this meeting could affect future monetary policy decisions.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves positively if the Federal Reserve publishes a statement indicating a cut in the upper bound of the target federal funds rate at the September 16-17, 2025 meeting. Resolution source: [Federal Reserve FOMC Calendars](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm). The level and change of the target federal funds rate will also be confirmed at the official website of the Federal Reserve: [Federal Reserve Open Market](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm).
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question as a rate cut at the September meeting would indicate a key decision by the FOMC, potentially setting the tone for the subsequent meetings in 2025.

question: Will Italy win the third most gold medals in the 2026 Winter Olympics?
description:
This market will resolve according to the country that wins the third most gold medals at the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics, scheduled for February 6-22, 2026.

In the case of ties, the ordered list for most gold medals won will use most overall medals won as a tiebreaker (e.g. If Norway and China tie for most gold medals won, and Norway wins more overall medals than China, Norway will be ranked first and China will be second). If this also results in a tie, the country whose name comes first in alphabetical order, as listed in this market group, will be ranked higher.

This market will resolve based on the medal figures as they stand after medals are awarded for the final event in the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics. Later changes to medal counts will not be considered toward the resolution of this market.

If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are partially completed and then cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve based on the gold medals awarded in the completed events. If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are entirely cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The resolution source will be official information from the International Olympic Committee (https://www.olympics.com/).

question: Will Rodrigo Paz Pereira win by 15–20%?
description:
A second-round (runoff) vote for the Bolivia Presidential election is scheduled to take place on October 19, 2025 

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the second round of the 2025 Bolivian Presidential Election.

For the purpose of this market, the 'margin of victory' is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first and second-place candidate. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the second round of the Bolivian Presidential Election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher placed bracket (ascending).

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the vote count has been made official.

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

If the results of the election aren’t known by March 31, 2026 ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

This market will resolve solely based on the first official vote count released by the Bolivian Government, specifically the Plurinational Electoral Body (Órgano Electoral Plurinacional, OEP) (https://www.oep.org.bo/).

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

question: Will Silver (SI) hit (HIGH) $110 by end of June?
description:

The Active Month becomes a non-active month effective on its First Position Date, at which point the next eligible contract month becomes the Active Month.

Only the Active Month's official settlement price published by CME Group will be considered. Intraday trades, highs, lows, bids, offers, midpoint values, or indicative prices do not count.

Note that the settlement price may differ from the last traded price. CME's methodology to determine the settlement price can vary by commodity and contract.

This market will resolve based on the settlement price as it appears on the CME settlement page at the time it is first published for that trading day, regardless of any later corrections or updates.

The resolution source for this market is the CME Group website — specifically, the daily "Settlement" price for the Active Month of Silver (SI) futures.

question: Will the Fed Pause–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Dec–Jan–Mar)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: December 9–10, 2025; January 27–28, 2026; and March 17-18, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other". Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the March 2026 meeting by April 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.rationale: The outcome of the December 2025 FOMC meeting is a key early indicator of the FOMC's stance on interest rate decisions, potentially influencing the subsequent meetings in January and March 2026.

question: Will the Fed Cut–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Oct–Dec–Jan)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: October 28–29, 2025; December 9–10, 2025; and January 27–28, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the January 2026 meeting by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.question: Will the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) announce a cut, pause, or hike in the target federal funds range at their next meeting on October 28–29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: At the next FOMC meeting, the committee will decide on the target federal funds range, potentially including a cut, pause, or hike based on their assessment of economic conditions. This decision will form the basis for subsequent market expectations and financial asset pricing. subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves positively if the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) announces a cut, pause, or hike in the target federal funds range at their meeting on October 28–29, 2025, as published in the official FOMC statement available at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant as the outcome of the FOMC meeting on October 28–29 will provide an early indicator of the Fed's monetary policy trajectory, which can influence the ultimate question of whether the Fed will Cut–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions.

question: Will BLS stop reporting payroll data this year?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) ceases regular publication of any of the following reports: monthly Employment Situation reports (nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate), Consumer Price Index (CPI), Producer Price Index (PPI), Employment Cost Index, Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS), by December 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No."

For purposes of this market, “ceases regular publication” means any of the following:

- The BLS officially announces it will no longer publish the report on its regular schedule.
- The BLS misses three consecutive scheduled releases of the report without providing the data within 30 days of each scheduled release date.
- The BLS announces that the report is discontinued, terminated, or permanently suspended.
- Legislative or executive action explicitly prohibits or defunds the publication of the report.

The following do NOT qualify as cessation:
- Temporary delays or postponements followed by subsequent publication (including delays caused by government shutdowns).
- Changes in methodology, seasonal adjustment, or calculation methods while continuing publication.
- Changes in publication frequency (e.g., monthly to quarterly) while maintaining regular releases.
- Format changes (e.g., digital-only, layout changes).
- Publishing preliminary or partial data with full data forthcoming.
- Changes to specific components within a report while the overall data series continues.
- Combining the report with other reports while still publishing the underlying data.
- BLS delays the jobs report due to a shutdown, then publishes it.
- BLS changes CPI methodology but continues publishing monthly CPI.
- BLS shifts employment data from monthly to quarterly.
- The Federal Reserve begins publishing employment data while BLS continues its own.
- BLS website outage delays posting, but data is released via other channels.
- BLS publishes preliminary data pending final adjustments.

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) officially announce the discontinuation or termination of any key economic reports by October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: On September 29, 2025, the U.S. Labor and Commerce departments warned that a potential partial government shutdown could halt key economic data releases, including employment reports and inflation figures. The Department of Labor's 73-page contingency plan stated that if the U.S. government shuts down, the BLS will 'suspend all operations' and cease all data-collection activities, potentially delaying or discontinuing the upcoming jobs report, nonfarm payrolls, the daily consumer price index (CPI) on October 15, and the producer price index on October 16. The plan noted that 'Economic data that are scheduled to be released during the lapse will not be released,' and that 'all active data collection activities for BLS surveys will cease,' potentially impacting the accuracy of future estimates and the Social Security Administration's Cost-of-Living Adjustment announcement.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Bureau of Labor Statistics officially announces the discontinuation or termination of any key economic reports by October 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET. Any announcement made after this date does not count towards the resolution. The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting regarding the official announcement of discontinuation or termination, or lack thereof. If multiple credible news sources report conflicting information about the announcement status, resolution will be based on the predominant conclusion from these sources. If there is no clarity in the reporting, the question will be deemed unresolved.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant as it directly addresses the potential discontinuation or termination of key economic reports by the BLS, which aligns with the ultimate question of whether BLS will stop reporting payroll data this year. An official announcement of such discontinuation or termination would serve as a significant indicator of the ultimate outcome.

question: Will Maduro's rule survive a US military engagement?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if both of the following conditions are met. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

1. There is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify as a military engagement. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count as a military engagement; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not.

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify as a military engagement.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify as a military engagement regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify as a military engagement (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

2. President Nicolás Maduro is NOT removed from power within the first 30 days after such an engagement ends, with no subsequent engagement occurring.

President Nicolás Maduro will be considered to be removed from power if he resigns, is detained, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as President of Venezuela within this market's timeframe.

A military engagement which occurs will be considered to have ended once no qualifying incidents occur for 24 consecutive hours following the initial engagement. The relevant thirty day period will begin on the calendar day following this 24 hours. If multiple military engagements occur, the 30-day period will be counted from the first day following the ending of the most recent engagement.

If Maduro is removed from power prior to a qualifying military engagement occurring this market will immediately resolve to "No".

Note: If a qualifying military engagement occurs by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will remain open until either Maduro is removed from power or a thirty day period has passed with no subsequent military engagements occurring. 

The primary source of resolution for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

question: U.S. x Russia Nuclear deal by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if an official agreement on nuclear arms control or strategic nuclear weapons limitation is reached between the United States and the Russian Federation between August 14, 2025 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Only agreements that are publicly announced and acknowledged by both the U.S. and Russia will qualify. The agreement must pertain to nuclear arms control or limitation—such as a treaty, framework, or memorandum—addressing matters including (but not limited to) nuclear warheads, delivery systems, verification mechanisms, or strategic stability.

An extension, amendment, or replacement of the New START treaty will qualify, provided it is publicly announced as a concluded agreement by both parties within the time frame. Exploratory discussions or stated intent to extend without a finalized agreement will not qualify.

Agreements that include both the United States and Russia as named parties—whether bilateral or as part of a broader multilateral framework—will qualify, provided the agreement directly addresses nuclear arms control.

The agreement does not need to be ratified or implemented for this market to resolve "Yes"; a formal announcement of a concluded agreement is sufficient.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements from the U.S. government (e.g., the White House, State Department) and/or the Russian Federation (e.g., the Kremlin, Ministry of Foreign Affairs). However, a clear and overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming that such an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will the United States and Russia publicly announce the extension, amendment, or replacement of the New START treaty before November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Russian President Vladimir Putin has unilaterally proposed to extend the New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (New START) with the United States for one year, beyond the treaty's expiration in February 2026. The New START treaty, signed in 2010, limits each party to no more than 700 deployed ICBMs, SLBMs, and strategic bombers and 1,550 warheads on deployed platforms. Regardless of the extension, amendment, or replacement of the New START treaty, the agreement must be publicly announced and acknowledged by both the U.S. and Russia before November 30, 2025, to qualify.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the extension, amendment, or replacement of the New START treaty is publicly announced and acknowledged by both the U.S. and Russia between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30. The primary resolution source will be official statements from the U.S. government (e.g., the White House, State Department) and/or the Russian Federation (e.g., the Kremlin, Ministry of Foreign Affairs). However, a clear and overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming that such an agreement has been reached will also qualify. Additional authoritative sources such as reputable news outlets will be consulted to confirm the announcement and acknowledgment.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question as it directly pertains to the extension, amendment, or replacement of the New START treaty, which is a significant aspect of U.S. x Russia nuclear deal discussions. The resolution of this subquestion will provide a key indicator of progress towards a comprehensive nuclear arms control agreement between the United States and Russia.

question: Will Russia enter Borova by December 31?
description:

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Any mode that requires a licensed driver to be seated in the vehicle, or for a human (on-site or remote) to continuously supervise the driving performance or remain ready to intervene at any moment, will not qualify. question: U.S. agrees to give Ukraine security guarantee in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States formally commits to giving Ukraine a security guarantee, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed deal between the Trump administration and the Government of Ukraine which creates a binding obligation for the United States to defend or directly intervene on Ukraine’s behalf, by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

A qualifying “security guarantee” requires language that is equivalent in character to a NATO Article 5–style mutual defense commitment: the United States must commit to responding militarily if Ukraine is attacked, or otherwise guarantee Ukraine’s defense through binding defense obligations. Examples of qualifying language include commitments modeled on the US treaties with Japan, South Korea, or the Philippines, or NATO's Article 5 instrument, which obligates the United States to “act to meet the common danger” through military force if an ally is attacked. Cooperative frameworks, capacity-building measures, consultative mechanisms, or nonbinding pledges will not qualify. 

Examples of non-qualifying arrangements include the June 13, 2024 US–Ukraine bilateral security agreement, the Taiwan Relations Act, or G7/EU “security arrangements” that provide support or consultation but stop short of binding defense guarantees.

A qualifying agreement must be jointly announced and finalized, and take the form of a treaty, executive agreement, memorandum of understanding, joint declaration, or equivalent written instrument. Announcements which are statements of intent, contingent, exploratory, or otherwise not indicative of a formalized policy will not count. 

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.background_information: On August 22, 2025, the U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Andrii Yermak, head of the Office of the President of Ukraine, held discussions on security guarantees for Ukraine. The plan involved political-legal and military groups working on guarantees, including weapons supply, financial support, intelligence sharing, and joint training missions. The draft project of security guarantees was planned to be finalized by the end of next week. Moreover, there have been discussions at global summits, with expectations for the U.S. to provide robust and credible security guarantees to Ukraine. The U.S. has also issued a similar security guarantee to Qatar, which referenced NATO's Article 5, indicating their willingness to provide binding defense obligations. These events provide context for the ongoing discussions and negotiations between the U.S. and Ukraine regarding a potential security agreement.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves positively if credible reports confirm the finalization and public announcement of a binding defense agreement equivalent in character to a NATO Article 5-style mutual defense commitment between the U.S. and Ukraine before November 30, 2025. Credible sources for resolution may include major international news agencies, official statements from the U.S. State Department, the Ukrainian government, or other recognized national authorities or declarations.
subquestions.rationale: The question aims to assess the progress of U.S.-Ukraine discussions on security guarantees, specifically focusing on the likelihood of finalizing a binding defense agreement equivalent to a NATO Article 5-style mutual defense commitment. question: Will Tesla launch a driverless Robotaxi service in 2025?
description:

Any service that allows a member of the general public to summon and ride in a Tesla vehicle operating without any human—onboard or remote—actively controlling the vehicle will count. A human may be present in the vehicle or monitoring remotely for emergency intervention, but they must not be physically positioned to take control (for example, no safety driver in the driver’s seat) and must not actively steer, brake, accelerate, or otherwise drive the car under normal operation.

A program that is restricted to Tesla employees, invite-only testers, closed-beta participants, factory self-delivery features, or the mere release of Full Self-Driving software for private owner-drivers will not qualify. Regulatory permits or approvals, press demonstrations, and prototype unveilings without live public ridership likewise will not count toward resolution.

This market’s resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla launch a fully driverless taxi service in Austin, Texas, by September 8, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Reports indicate that Tesla has launched a robotaxi service in Austin, Texas, as part of a limited and carefully monitored trial. The service includes a small number of Model Y vehicles operated in a geofenced area within the city limits. The vehicles are using Full Self-Driving (FSD) software which is under the supervision of a 'safety monitor' in the front passenger seat. The presence of the safety monitor contradicts Elon Musk's original promise of unsupervised rides. Additionally, there have been regulatory challenges in Texas related to the launch of driverless vehicles, with new laws mandating a permit to operate self-driving vehicles set to take effect on September 1, 2025.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if credible reports confirm the public launch of a fully driverless Tesla robotaxi service in Austin, Texas, without any human actively controlling the vehicle, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08. Resolution will be based on reports from authoritative sources such as major news outlets or official Tesla announcements. Sources: [1] CNA - https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/business/texas-enacts-robotaxi-rules-eve-tesla-austin-rollout-1551352, [2] Popular Mechanics - https://www.popularmechanics.com/cars/a40564133/elon-musk-promised-driverless-taxis-instead-you-get-a-guy-in-the-passenger-seat/

question: Will there be no US government shutdown by January 31 and will the Republican Party win the House in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the combined outcome of whether there will be another US government shutdown by January 31 (https://polymarket.com/event/will-there-be-another-us-government-shutdown-by-january-31?) and according to which party will win the House in 2026 (https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-house-in-2026?).

The rules and resolution criteria are as follows:

1. Will there be another US government shutdown by January 31?
This market will resolve according to whether the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announces another federal government shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Partial shutdowns count as shutdowns; announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather do not qualify as a shutdown.

The resolution source for this market will be OPM’s Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/).

2. Which party will win the House in 2026?
This market will resolve according to the party that controls the House of Representatives following the 2026 U.S. House elections scheduled for November 3, 2026.

House control is defined as having more than half of the voting members of the U.S. House of Representatives.

If the outcome of this election is ambiguous given the above rules, this market will remain open until the Speaker of the House is selected following the 2026 U.S. general election, at which point it will resolve to the party the Speaker is affiliated with at the time of their election to that position. If the elected Speaker does not caucus with any listed party this market will resolve “Other”.

Determination of which party controls the House after the 2026 U.S. House elections will be based on a consensus of credible reporting, or if there is ambiguity, final federal and/or state election authority certification or other final official determination of the 2026 election results.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announce another federal government shutdown by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET?
subquestions.background_information: Recent news articles indicate the possibility of another government shutdown if Congress fails to pass necessary spending bills by the deadline. Bipartisan negotiations and disputes over funding, particularly related to the Affordable Care Act's enhanced subsidies, have raised concerns about a potential lapse in appropriations. The failure to secure funding could result in a federal government shutdown, affecting the functioning of multiple federal agencies.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves positively if the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) officially announces a federal government shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations between 2026-01-09 and 2026-01-31. The resolution will use OPM’s Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/) as the primary source of confirmation.
subquestions.rationale: The announcement of a federal government shutdown by the U.S. Office of Personnel Management would be a crucial early indicator of the likelihood of a government shutdown by January 31, 2026.
